newsitem.title: HUNGARY: INVESTORS IN HUNGARY ENERGY CONCERNED AFTER TALKS.
newsitem.headline: INVESTORS IN HUNGARY ENERGY CONCERNED AFTER TALKS.

text.p: Western investors in Hungary's energy sector said they were still concerned about government plans to increase energy prices in January following talks with government ministers on Wednesday.

"We weren't given enough detail to be able to evaluate the whole situation but we do have some concerns," a representative of the US consortium AES, a majority shareholder in the Tisza power station, told Reuters as he came out of the talks.
"We are interested in making sure that price levels are sufficient that there is additional investment in the industry (but) we don't know yet," the spokesman, who declined to be named, said.
The government is expected to announce on Thursday the amount by which energy suppliers and distributors should be allowed to put up energy prices on January 1.

Western utilities such as French giant Gaz de France and German electricity company RWE , who bought large stakes in Hungary's energy distribution companies a year ago are concerned that the rise will not ensure them an eight-percent return on investment promised to them.

Representatioves of all the investors on Wednesday held a final round of negotiations with a government commissioner, Imre Karl, appointed to review pricing policy, privatisation minister Judit Csiha and industry minister Szabolcs Fazakas.
Press reports on Tuesday said Karl was recommending that gas be raised by 16 percent and electricity by 23 percent.

Pierre Abou, Electricite de France's representative in Hungary said nothing was finalised in the meeting but he hoped that the government would not postpone the decision, as they did with a planned rise for October.
"These were just talks," he told Reuters. "The decision will take place tomorrow and we hope the government will make up its mind to make the right decision."

Industry minister Fazakas told Reuters there would be no difference between the information shared with the investors and what Hungary's Cabinet will discuss on Thursday but he declined to reveal figures.
"We informed the investors about the proposal Commissioner Karl has prepared and we will submit the same propsal to the goverment tomorrow," Fazakas said.
